name: Zendesk
description: Widely used customer service and ticketing platform with a broad suite of support, messaging, and voice APIs.
gating_notes: Free trial accounts are available self-serve and include full API access; API tokens can be generated directly from admin settings without sales involvement. OAuth apps (public/marketplace) go through an app review process.
mcp_notes: Zendesk runs an official per-tenant MCP server at https://<subdomain>.zendesk.com/api/mcp (OAuth, read/write scopes), plus several community MCP servers on GitHub (e.g. reminia/zendesk-mcp-server, michaelrice/zendesk-mcp).

name: Intercom
description: Customer messaging and support platform (now positioned around Fin AI agent) with a REST API for conversations, contacts, and companies.
gating_notes: Developers can self-serve create a private app and generate an access token via the Developer Hub, but this requires an active (paid) Intercom workspace — access tokens grant access to 'your paid Intercom workspace' data. A trial workspace can be used to test. Public OAuth apps require Developer Hub setup but no sales gate mentioned.
mcp_notes: Official remote MCP server at https://mcp.intercom.com/mcp with 13 tools (conversations, contacts, companies, Help Center articles), OAuth-scoped, available for US and EU hosted workspaces (not yet AU).

name: Freshdesk
description: Cloud helpdesk/ticketing software (Freshworks) with a broad REST API covering tickets, contacts, companies, and automations.
gating_notes: API key is available directly from the support portal profile page; trial accounts get a default rate limit (50 calls/min) and can use the API immediately with no sales approval.
mcp_notes: Freshworks shipped an official MCP integration for Freshdesk (GA as of Sept 2026), plus community servers such as NeuraLegion/freshdesk_mcp (41 tools) and Enreign/freshdeck-mcp.

name: Front
description: Shared-inbox customer communication platform with a REST Core API plus webhooks, connectors, and a plugin SDK.
gating_notes: Developers can sign up for a free developer environment and generate API tokens directly from account settings for testing/internal integrations; public/marketplace integrations are steered toward OAuth and generally require Front's exception/approval to publish, but building and testing is self-serve.
mcp_notes: Front has an official beta MCP server at mcp.frontapp.com/mcp (OAuth-scoped, teammate-permission-bound) plus a community server (zqushair/Frontapp-MCP).

name: Pylon
description: B2B customer support platform (issues, Slack-based support, account intelligence) with a REST API and admin-issued tokens.
gating_notes: API tokens can only be created by Admin users, and third-party pricing trackers report that API access is only available starting on the Professional tier (paid, 3-seat minimum, ~$89/seat/mo), not on any free/self-serve tier.
mcp_notes: Official remote MCP server at https://mcp.usepylon.com (Streamable HTTP, OAuth-based, configured via Settings > AI Controls > MCP Server) for issues, accounts, and contacts.
blocker: API/admin token access appears gated behind a paid Professional-tier plan rather than a free self-serve trial, based on third-party pricing sources (not directly confirmed on usepylon.com pricing page).

name: LiveAgent
description: Help desk / live chat software with a REST API (v3) for tickets, agents, and configuration, accessed via per-account API keys.
gating_notes: API keys are generated by an admin directly in Configuration > System > API within any LiveAgent account (including free trial accounts), no sales approval needed.
mcp_notes: LiveAgent has a built-in MCP integration (Settings/Agents area) plus a community MCP server (QualityUnit/liveagent-mcp-server on GitHub).

name: Plain
description: API-first B2B support/ticketing tool built around a GraphQL API, designed for engineering-led support workflows.
gating_notes: Entry-level Foundation plan ($35/seat/mo) explicitly supports self-serve setup with a 7-day free trial (no credit card); API keys are generated by the account owner without sales contact.
mcp_notes: Official MCP server at https://mcp.plain.com/mcp, documented at plain.com/docs/agents/mcp-server, using OAuth scoped to the connecting user's permissions.

name: Help Scout
description: Email-based helpdesk platform with Mailbox (Inbox), Docs, Beacon, and Chat APIs, all authenticated via OAuth2.
auth_methods: OAuth2 (Authorization Code and Client Credentials flows)
gating_notes: Any account holder can create an OAuth2 app themselves via Profile > My apps; Help Scout offers a free trial account which is sufficient to register an app and pull credentials without sales involvement.
mcp_notes: No official Help Scout MCP server found, but several active community servers exist (drewburchfield/help-scout-mcp-server and forks by GravityKit, WayLit, BusyBee3333).

name: Gorgias
description: E-commerce-focused helpdesk (deep Shopify/BigCommerce integration) with a REST API for tickets, customers, and automation.
auth_methods: API key (Basic auth) for private apps
gating_notes: REST API credentials (base URL, email, API key) are available directly from Settings > Account > REST API on any account, including trial accounts; public OAuth apps require Gorgias approval to be listed, but private-app API-key access needs no approval.
mcp_notes: Official MCP server at mcp.gorgias.com/mcp, included on every helpdesk plan (currently in beta); community servers also exist (e.g. cacosat/gorgias, benpalmer1/Gorgias-MCP-Server).

name: Gladly
description: Enterprise customer-service platform centered on a lifelong customer conversation timeline, mainly sold to large retail/CX teams.
auth_methods: unknown (API reference at developer.gladly.com was not directly accessible; likely API key/OAuth token per standard app platform patterns)
gating_notes: No public self-serve signup or pricing for the core platform — evaluation requires booking a demo/sales engagement, and the platform is enterprise-contract only (reported deployments in the $100K-$500K+/year range). A separate self-serve 'Sidekick for Shopify' product has a free trial, but that is a narrower AI product, not general platform API access.
mcp_notes: No official Gladly MCP server found; a third-party managed connector (StackOne) offers a Gladly MCP server with 65 actions, which implies an underlying REST API exists but isn't independently documented here.
blocker: No self-serve developer signup or public API docs were reachable; API access appears to require an existing paid enterprise contract and sales relationship, making it hard for Composio to build/test a toolkit without a customer account.
